original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: An opt-in endpoint-event sweep constructs exactly the same elementary mirror windows as PR4483 while classifying each target/paid rank pair once. Exact full-output conformance and enumerated classification counts are certified.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a measured replay speedup. This scoped contribution instead proves an exact reduction in repeated pair classifications and supplies complete interface conformance. It does not claim a wall-time speedup or identify the complete caller bottleneck; those remain explicit next questions.
bottleneck_link: Exact mirror histograms are reused in compiler admission inequalities. The sweep removes repeated pair classification while preserving every cell, product-rank multiplicity and source-funding rejection. It does not change native work or supplier admission.
stop_rule: Ship the first exact reduction in repeated classifications. Do not tune additional kernels or infer a runtime speedup from operation counts.
evidence: PROOF.md, windows.py and verify.py: complete output equality on 6400 histogram pairs and retained p7/p16 inputs, exact endpoint/ownership/collision controls, and classification counts 1296 to 81 and 4550 to 182.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Does explicit adoption of the sweep reduce an actual complete compiler replay time?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Fewer pair classifications do not measure total runtime; output copying and exact powers may dominate.
open_questions.first_step: Install the opt-in function in one isolated current compiler caller and perform a fair end-to-end benchmark with every output and rejection preserved.
open_questions.blocked_by: No shared/default adoption or full-caller timing is supplied.

open_questions.question: Can consumers reuse endpoint events without materializing every full histogram?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The current implementation pays to copy each emitted source/exit histogram, so its total work includes output size.
open_questions.first_step: Specify an incremental exact moment consumer and compare its complete interval output with the materialized interface.
open_questions.blocked_by: A changed consumer contract needs separate proof and source binding.
